issues.description: Inner blocking read loop has no timeout or process-exit check, deadlocking if writer never closes the FIFO.
issues.detail: Once O_NONBLOCK is cleared and control enters the inner while-True os.read(), the outer poll timeout and check_process_exited safeguards no longer apply. A hung child, stuck flush, or inherited writer fd in a grandchild leaves the reader blocked forever. The patch trades an intermittent truncation race for a guaranteed deadlock on writer hang.

issues.description: POSIX EOF guarantee silently assumes a single writer with no inherited fds; precondition is unstated.
issues.detail: Blocking read returns 0 only when all write ends are closed. If any process (including a grandchild that inherited the fd) still holds the writer, the loop blocks indefinitely. The cited POSIX guarantee is weaker than the comment claims, and the loop invariant and precondition are nowhere written down.

issues.description: fcntl mode flip is not restored via try/finally; descriptor is silently mutated for any caller that reuses it.
issues.detail: The function clears O_NONBLOCK on fifo_fd as a side effect with no try/finally to restore state on exception. The frame condition on the descriptor is not documented, so an exception between F_SETFL and the inner loop leaks blocking state to subsequent callers.

issues.description: BlockingIOError handler is now dead or unreasoned after the mode switch.
issues.detail: Once the fd is in blocking mode, BlockingIOError on that read is impossible, yet the handler remains and silently does pass. Either it is dead code or evidence the author has not characterised which fd states reach it. State the postcondition or delete the branch.

issues.description: No regression test exercises the original race or the new blocking-drain path.
issues.detail: The PR cites an intermittent JSONDecodeError at char 86672 but adds no fixture writing more than 64KB then exiting immediately, and no test that the blocking-drain path is actually entered. Correctness rests on prose and a POSIX appeal rather than evidence. A deterministic test would convert the proof into demonstration.

issues.description: Two coupled read loops with different EOF semantics complect the protocol; framing on the writer side is the simpler fix.
issues.detail: The function now runs a non-blocking outer loop and a blocking inner loop, each with its own EOF logic, bypassing the outer poll machinery once data arrives. The root cause is an unframed IPC: a length-prefixed or newline-delimited write on the producer side would make EOF detection non-load-bearing and let the reader stay simple.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the patch correctly identifies a real race between non-blocking reads and kernel pipe buffering, but trades it for a worse failure mode: the new inner blocking-read loop has no timeout, no poll, and no process-exit check, so a hung writer now deadlocks the reader instead of timing out. Correctness rests on an unstated invariant and a POSIX EOF guarantee that silently assumes a single writer with no inherited fds. Secondary issues: the fcntl mode flip lacks try/finally, the BlockingIOError branch is dead or unreasoned post-switch, and no regression test exercises either the original race or the new blocking path. The cleaner fix is writer-side framing, not reader-side tolerance of an underspecified protocol.
